title: CrowdStrike to shell out nearly $500M for 2 AI security startups as the market for securing agents takes off
slides: Why is CrowdStrike paying nearly $500M now?
Two AI security startups acquired in one move
But the real target is securing AI agents themselves
Your AI agents may soon need identity and access controls
Audit what agents can access before attackers do
thread_text:
1. $500M for AI security

CrowdStrike is paying nearly half a billion dollars to acquire two AI security startups. The deal isn't about today's tools — it's a bet on what comes next.

2. Two startups, one move

CrowdStrike isn't buying one company — it's buying two AI security startups in a single deal. That's not a talent grab, it's a strategy shift.

3. The real target

The acquisitions aren't about securing AI models. They're about securing AI agents — the autonomous programs that act on your behalf. That's a much harder problem.

4. Agents need ID checks

Your AI agents will soon need identity and access controls, just like human employees. Without them, any agent can act as anyone — and no one will know.

5. Audit before attackers

List every system your AI agents can access today. If you can't answer that in five minutes, you have a gap an attacker will find first.
